beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: SOLIPSCION opens with a child learning to make rain by influencing another world.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: She may nudge existing conditions, but cannot simply suspend its local laws.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Her chosen route uses fear to move a herd toward a hidden reservoir.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The tutor questions more than whether the intervention produces the intended result.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: This speculative novel alternates powerful children with lives inside the worlds they affect.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its particular tension is the distance between an educational objective and someone's actual experience.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The lower perspective makes its world more than a surface for an exercise.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Observers there have bodies, relationships, cities, and difficult evidence to interpret.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: An astronomer's attention can matter without revealing the larger system around that life.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The alternating viewpoints let the reader understand more than either participant alone.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That advantage also creates responsibility for what a distant explanation leaves out.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book develops its metaphysics through the unequal positions of people who must act.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The journey moves through worlds whose inhabitants confront different forms of scarcity and dependence.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Water distribution and limited care do not feel like interchangeable educational problems from within.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The children also inhabit a system that interprets their progress through its own measures.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That double dependence complicates an easy division between powerful operators and powerless subjects.
